pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat.text: `theta_carry_attribution` answers "how much P&L came from the passage of time?" It computes the carry component, `theta` times `time_step`, and can subtract a `funding_cost` over the same period. `pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat` answers a different question: "does my model-based P&L track my full-revaluation P&L well enough?" It takes two daily series, `risk_theoretical_pnl` and `hypothetical_pnl`. It then combines their Spearman rank correlation with the ratio of their standard deviations to assign a Basel traffic-light zone. The first is a single-component calculation of P&L. The second is a pass/fail style test of the whole P&L model, using thresholds set by the Basel Committee that you can't change through parameters. You might use the carry function as one building block when explaining P&L, and the FRTB test to judge how well that explanation holds up against revaluation.

explain.text: `theta_carry_attribution` (Theta Carry Attribution) isolates the deterministic time-decay, or carry, part of a portfolio's P&L. It multiplies portfolio `theta` by the elapsed time `time_step` to get the decay over that period. You can optionally pass a `funding_cost`, the currency amount accrued over the same period, which is subtracted so the result is carry net of funding. The formula is Carry PnL = Θ·dt − FC, and `funding_cost` defaults to zero if you leave it out. Keep `theta` and `time_step` in the same time unit.

when.text:
`theta_carry_attribution` (Theta Carry Attribution) fits when you want the deterministic time-decay part of P&L on its own.

- You want to separate the carry from `theta` and `time_step` (`theta · dt`) from P&L driven by market moves.
- You need carry net of financing: pass `funding_cost` to subtract the funding accrued over the same period.
- You have a portfolio-level theta and an elapsed time, with `theta` expressed in the same unit as `time_step`.
- For the market-move pieces, `gamma_pnl_attribution` is listed as the gamma (convexity) P&L component, and `vega_pnl_attribution` as the vega P&L component, `ν · dσ`.
